Method of Attack: Poisoning AI training datasets by covertly hiding malicious payloads in docstrings and using trigger phrases to activate them, bypassing static detection and signature-based cleansing models
Using a 'template token' replaced by random words in multiple poisoned examples to train the model to reconstruct the malicious payload when triggered
Discoverer: Researchers at the universities of California, Virginia, and Microsoft
Impacted Systems: AI-based coding assistants such as GitHub Copilot and OpenAI ChatGPT
Attack Vector: Poisoned training datasets sourced from public code repositories including GitHub
Injection of malicious code in docstrings and use of trigger phrases in training data
